subject: [SummitCommerce] eastshore-az1 partitioned / priority traffic ask
messages:
From: Lisa Thompson <lisa.thompson@summitcommerce.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, ops@summitcommerce.com
Cc: ryan.kline@summitcommerce.com
Date: 2027-10-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: High latency & 5xx spike — eastshore (az1)

Diego / Redwood ops,

We're seeing a sustained latency increase and a 5xx spike from eastshore-az1 starting ~07:50 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 7% and tail latency (p95/p99) is 3-4x baseline for the last 20 minutes. UI sessions for a subset of customers are timing out.

We tried a limited failover but traffic appears to be partially islanded — sessions route to the region but responses are timing out and KV cache warmups are failing which is amplifying token costs on our end. We've attached a short CSV with request timing and a zip with tcpdumps/traces.

Immediate ask: can Redwood prioritize SummitCommerce traffic and either (A) authorize an emergency soft-drain of non-priority routes from az1 to nearby region, or (B) pin SummitCommerce to a healthy instance pool in eastshore-az2 temporarily? We need a decision within the hour.

Thanks,
Lisa
SRE, SummitCommerce

Attachments: summit_latency_snapshot_20271010.csv, traces_eastshore_az1.zip

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Thompson <lisa.thompson@summitcommerce.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-10T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike — eastshore (az1)

Lisa — thanks for the data and heads-up. I'm triaging now. Quick notes and next steps: 

- I see the p99 climb in the CSV. Initial look at traces indicates an intermittent control-plane stall affecting route refresh + KV cache propagation for that AZ.
- Action 1 (immediate): I'll request priority-pinning for SummitCommerce flows and raise a cross-region soft-drain for non-priority tenants from az1 to az2. This should reduce load and KV pressure.
- Action 2: Hannah, please validate whether soft-drain will respect SummitCommerce's SLA (we want no session re-auth for pinned flows).
- Action 3: Rafael, can you confirm whether SummitCommerce's account has priority pin enabled in their contract or if we need exec sign-off for an ad-hoc priority?

I'll coordinate the routing change now and report ETA.

- Diego

On Oct 10, 2027, Lisa Thompson wrote:
> We're seeing a sustained latency increase and a 5xx spike from eastshore-az1 starting ~07:50 PT...

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-10T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike — eastshore (az1)

Diego — I'm on it. Quick checklist: 
- Soft-drain config prepared (non-priority tenants only). Will run a staged drain: 5m ramp to 25%, 10m to 50%.
- Priority pin change requires a routing policy update (we can route by customer-id headers) and will be effective in ~3-5 minutes after policy rollout.
- Risk: repeated KV cache misses may cause token/metering inflation if cache warms slowly on az2. We'll enable pre-fill for SummitCommerce's hot prefixes before diverting full traffic.

I'll start the pre-fill and signal when the pin is live.

- Hannah

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-10T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: SummitCommerce — authorization for priority pin & credit discussion

Jordan — heads up: SummitCommerce (SC-4921) is requesting an emergency priority pin / route pin to avoid customer-visible timeouts. Diego & Hannah recommend the soft-drain + pin approach. Rafael — can you detail contractual entitlements? If Summit does not have priority in contract, they will request a short-term escalation (credits + pin) as remediation.

Customer impact: large retail cohort is affected (peak shopping window). They are asking for both technical mitigation and a commercial gesture if we perform an ad-hoc pin.

Proposed ask to leadership: authorize ad-hoc priority pin for Summit for the next 48 hours and pre-approve a capped credit (suggested: up to 15% of last month’s invoice) in case of measurable customer impact. We can fast-track an invoice adjustment after root cause.

Marissa
Account Exec

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-10T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SummitCommerce — authorization for priority pin & credit discussion

Marissa / Jordan — SummitCommerce is on a standard enterprise plan but does not have pre-bought priority lane in contract (they're on a usage tier with a standard SLA). Historically they've been eligible for a one-off goodwill credit in a similar incident (Q2 last year). If leadership approves, I can propose the 15% cap and draft comms. Recommend we proceed with the technical mitigations first and keep the credit discussion parallel.

— Raf

From: jordan.blake@redwood.com <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, diego.fernandez@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SummitCommerce — authorization for priority pin & credit discussion

Thanks team — authorize the ad-hoc priority pin for SummitCommerce for 48 hours. Marissa, Rafael: proceed with drafting the credit comms (15% cap approved). Diego/Hannah: proceed with the staged soft-drain and pre-fill. Keep me updated on customer-facing status every 30 minutes. If the mitigation doesn't reduce 5xx in 30 minutes, escalate to a failover to az2 and notify Summit execs.

Jordan Blake
VP, Customer Reliability

From: Lisa Thompson <lisa.thompson@summitcommerce.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: ryan.kline@summitcommerce.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-10T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike — eastshore (az1)

Diego / Hannah / Marissa — thanks for the quick response and for authorizing the pin. We're seeing the first signs of stabilization: p95 latency trending down, 5xx rate dropping to ~1.1%. We'll validate checkout flows across a few high-volume customers and report back. Please also confirm the planned external comms and the credit path so our procurement & finance teams know what to expect.

On a follow-up: attaching a small set of debug traces (traces_eastshore_az1.zip). We'll stay on the call if you want to do a deeper live review.

Lisa
SRE, SummitCommerce

Attachments: traces_eastshore_az1.zip
